headline: Fine-particle pollution is Ward 40's strongest score, among the lowest readings citywide.
summary:
8.75 micrograms per cubic meter, Ward 40's fine-particle pollution reading, is among the lowest anywhere in Chicago. The ward covers Lincoln Square, West Ridge, Edgewater, and Rogers Park on the North Side, and lands 16th of 50 wards overall, just inside the city's top third. City government numbers also stand out here. The ward sponsored more non-routine legislation than most wards this session, and its aldermanic menu spending reaches a broader spread of projects than in most of the city.

The weaker spots are ozone levels, grocery access, and school funding. Ground-level ozone here lands among the worst readings of the fifty wards, a different kind of air pollution than the fine particles the ward does well on. Licensed grocery stores per resident are also scarce, among the lowest counts in Chicago. Per-pupil school spending sits in the bottom ten wards. The overall rank of 16 lands a little ahead of what these specific weak spots suggest. This is a ward that beats most of Chicago on some kinds of air pollution but falls behind on food access and school funding.
reading_the_rankings: A couple of these rankings are softer than they look. Resident metric ideas submitted to Ward Wise Explorer put the ward 46th of 50, which reads like low civic engagement on its face, but two points is all that separates this ward from thirty-nine others here, and the middle band of all fifty wards on this question spans nothing at all, essentially zero points. Almost every ward submitted close to nothing, so 46th mostly reflects app use, not anything about the neighborhood. How much of Ward 40's menu dollars went toward relighting streets and alleys is the next number worth a caveat. That measure lands the ward 44th of 50, but the gap is mostly noise. Only two points keep this ranking apart from thirty-eight others in the city. This figure also carries a 2023 boundary redraw in its history, meaning older years counted a differently shaped ward. It also only exists for some of the fifty, since a handful of wards never reported a figure here at all. A rank this low barely separates Ward 40 from most of the city. Trust in local government looks like a real strength at 4th place, but the roster behind it is thinner than fifty wards, since not everyone turned in a trust score, so the ranking runs against whoever did answer, not the full field.

news.headline: Lincoln Square Apartment Plan Needs More Family Units, Less Parking, Neighbors Say
news.note: Neighbors at a community meeting hosted by the ward's office asked the developer of a proposed 37-unit building on West Lawrence Avenue to add more family-sized units and fewer parking spots.

news.headline: Rogers Park Affordable Apartments, West Ridge Dispensary Approved By City Council
news.note: City Council approved the ward's first dispensary, planned for a vacant commercial building at 2415 W. Peterson Ave. in West Ridge.

news.headline: Cary's Lounge Sold After 50+ Years As A Family Business, But New Owner Vows To Keep It The Same
news.note: A family-owned bar on Devon Avenue in West Ridge changed hands after more than 50 years, with the new owner planning to keep its character.
